context.analysis:
## Overview
The Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening System processes card-not-present payment authorizations to detect fraud within a sub-50ms latency window while providing case management for analysts. It ensures PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance and 7-year tamper-evident auditability within a strict budget and team size.

## Key Elements
- Cardholders / Merchants: External entities initiating transactions indirectly.
- Payment Gateway / Acquirer: External system sending authorization requests via REST/gRPC.
- Fraud Analysts & Risk Managers: Internal users accessing the system for case reviews and rule updates.
- Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening System: Core software system processing scores, rules, and audit logs.
- AWS ECS on Fargate: Container platform hosting the hot-path scoring engine.
- AWS QLDB / S3 Object Lock: Storage for tamper-evident audit logs.
- AWS Cognito: Identity provider handling OAuth2/OIDC and MFA.

## Relationships
- Payment Gateway to Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening System: Sends synchronous authorization requests using gRPC/HTTPS over mTLS.
- Fraud Analysts to Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening System: Accesses case management via HTTPS (TLS 1.3).
- Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening System to AWS QLDB / S3: Streams asynchronous audit logs for tamper-evident retention.
- Fraud Screening System to AWS ECS / Fargate: Executes scalable scoring containers for low-latency decisions.

## Technology Stack
- AWS ECS on Fargate: Chosen for containerized scalability supporting 3,000 TPS within the €25k/month budget.
- gRPC / HTTPS: Ensures high-throughput, low-latency communication satisfying the <50ms P99 performance SLA.
- AWS QLDB / S3 Object Lock: Implemented to guarantee tamper-evident, cryptographically verifiable 7-year audit retention.
- AWS Cognito & IAM: Enforces OAuth2/OIDC authentication and strict RBAC to isolate PCI-DSS boundaries.
- Terraform: Utilized for Infrastructure as Code to maintain immutable infrastructure and automated deployments.

## Rationale
This architecture balances strict sub-50ms latency and PCI-DSS compliance requirements by decoupling heavy audit logging from the synchronous hot path. Leveraging managed AWS services ensures high availability and fail-open resilience while remaining within the fixed €25k monthly budget and 3-engineer operational capacity.

containers.analysis:
## Overview
The Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening system evaluates card-not-present payment authorizations for fraud, returning approve, decline, or review decisions while providing case management for fraud analysts. It runs on AWS in the eu-west-1 region, meeting PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance within a 25,000 EUR monthly budget.

## Key Elements
- Cardholders / Merchants
- Fraud Analysts & Risk Managers
- Payment Gateway / Acquirer
- AWS Application Load Balancer (ALB)
- AWS ECS on Fargate (Scoring Engine and Case Management Service containers)
- Amazon DynamoDB
- AWS S3 Object Lock
- AWS Cognito

## Relationships
- Payment Gateway / Acquirer -> AWS Application Load Balancer (gRPC/HTTPS over mTLS)
- Fraud Analysts & Risk Managers -> Case Management Service (HTTPS, TLS 1.3 via AWS Cognito OAuth2/MFA)
- Scoring Engine -> Amazon DynamoDB (TCP for sub-10ms feature retrieval)
- Scoring Engine -> AWS S3 Object Lock (AWS API for asynchronous tamper-evident audit logging)

## Technology Stack
- AWS Application Load Balancer: Ingress layer providing low-latency routing without API Gateway overhead.
- Java (Spring Boot / gRPC) on AWS ECS on Fargate: Stateless scoring engine meeting <50ms P99 latency at 3,000 TPS.
- Node.js / React on AWS ECS on Fargate: Case management UI ensuring analysts never access raw card data.
- Amazon DynamoDB: Low-latency feature store for transaction evaluation.
- AWS S3 Object Lock: Tamper-evident 7-year audit storage replacing QLDB to minimize operational overhead.
- AWS Cognito: Identity provider handling OAuth2/OIDC and MFA for internal users.

## Rationale
This architecture achieves sub-50ms latency at 3,000 TPS within a fixed 25,000 EUR monthly budget by using stateless Fargate containers and direct ALB routing. It satisfies strict compliance, security, and 7-year auditability requirements via tokenization, S3 Object Lock, and an operational footprint manageable by a three-engineer team.

Scoring Engine.analysis:
## Overview
The Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening system processes card-not-present payment authorizations to detect and prevent fraud before approval while supporting real-time case management for analysts. It operates on AWS to meet strict performance, compliance, and budget requirements.

## Key Elements
- Cardholders / Merchants
- Fraud Analysts & Risk Managers
- Payment Gateway / Acquirer
- AWS Application Load Balancer (ALB)
- Scoring Engine (Java (Spring Boot / gRPC) on AWS ECS on Fargate)
  - gRPC Ingress Handler
  - Feature Evaluator Component
  - ML Inference & Rule Engine Component (with Shadow Evaluation Router)
  - Audit Dispatcher Component
- Case Management Service (Node.js / React on AWS ECS on Fargate)
- Amazon DynamoDB
- AWS S3 Object Lock
- AWS Cognito

## Relationships
- Payment Gateway / Acquirer -> AWS Application Load Balancer (ALB) via gRPC/HTTPS over mTLS
- Fraud Analysts & Risk Managers -> AWS Cognito via OAuth2/OIDC
- Fraud Analysts & Risk Managers -> Case Management Service via HTTPS (TLS 1.3)
- AWS Application Load Balancer (ALB) -> Scoring Engine via gRPC/HTTPS
- AWS Application Load Balancer (ALB) -> Case Management Service via HTTPS
- Scoring Engine -> Amazon DynamoDB via TCP
- Scoring Engine -> AWS S3 Object Lock via AWS API

## Technology Stack
- AWS ECS on Graviton2 Fargate: Minimizes OS patch management overhead while delivering predictable performance.
- Java (Spring Boot / gRPC) & ONNX Runtime: Provides high-throughput, low-latency transaction scoring and model inference.
- Amazon DynamoDB: Acts as a low-latency feature store for transaction evaluation.
- AWS S3 Object Lock: Ensures tamper-evident, 7-year audit storage.
- AWS Cognito: Handles secure identity management and authentication.

## Rationale
This architecture uses serverless containers on Graviton2 Fargate and managed AWS services to achieve <50ms P99 latency at 3,000 TPS within a 25,000 EUR monthly budget. It enforces PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance and 7-year tamper-evident auditability using isolated security controls and tokenized data flows.

## Overview
[The system provides real-time fraud screening for card-not-present payment authorizations, enabling automated risk decisions and analyst reviews. It ensures PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance while maintaining sub-50ms latency under high throughput.]

## Key Elements
- Cardholders / Merchants
- Fraud Analysts & Risk Managers
- Payment Gateway / Acquirer
- AWS Application Load Balancer (ALB)
- Scoring Engine (Java, Spring Boot, gRPC)
- Case Management Service (Node.js, React)

- Fraud Analysts & Risk Managers -> AWS Cognito (OAuth2/OIDC)

## Rationale

It empowers a three-engineer team to operate a high-throughput, low-latency financial system with minimal operational overhead.]

The Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening system screens card-not-present payment authorizations to approve, decline, or route them for review. It ensures 7-year tamper-evident auditability while adhering to PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance and a strict budget.

- Payment Gateway / Acquirer
